newsitem.title: USA: Republican offers to work with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Republican offers to work with Clinton.

text.p: Sen. Dirk Kempthorne of Idaho said Saturday Republicans were ready to work with President Clinton on environmental protection bills and other legislation during the next session of Congress.
"There are so many issues where consensus is possible," Kempthorne said in the Republican response to Clinton's weekly Saturday radio address.

"We can finally balance the budget, make Medicare able to meet the health care needs of our seniors and continue to improve educational opportunities for our young people. And, we can surely all work together to make our environment better in the 21st century," Kempthorne said.
Kempthorne said he hoped to reach a bipartisan agreement on a new law to protect endangered species without hurting economic growth.
"Can we rewrite the law to allow us to save species while balancing the needs of our communities? Well, we'd better," he said. "It's time to restore common sense to environmental laws."
"That's why I am determined to write a law that protects endangered species without putting communities and people at risk," he said.

The Endangered Species Act gives the government authority to take measures to protect the habitat of dwindling wildlife. Critics say it can infringe on private property owners' rights to develop their land or deny the timber, mining and other industries access to resources on federal lands.

"We need a law that recovers species, offers incentives, strengthens the responsibilities of states and encourages people with diverse interests to work together to protect wildlife and jobs," he said.
"Mr. President, the Republicans are ready to work with you and make this all a reality," Kempthorne said.
